ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects with the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{4}{x}$ ($x>0$) at points $A(m, 4)$ and $B(2, n)$. It also intersects with the coordinate axes at points $M$ and $N$. Based on the graph, write directly the solution set of the inequality $kx+b-\frac{4}{x}<0$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the graph, we directly obtain the solution set of the inequality $kx+b-\frac{4}{x}<0$ as $0<x<1$ or $x>2$.\\
Hence, the answer is $x\in(0,1)\cup(x>2)$.\\
Therefore, the solution set is $x\in\boxed{(0,1)\cup(2,\infty)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes; the graph of the inverse proportional function is a curve in the first quadrant decreasing toward the lower right; the linear function y=kx+b is a straight line slanting toward the lower right, intersecting the coordinate axes at M and N respectively, and intersecting the graph of the inverse proportional function at point A in the upper left and point B in the lower right. Reasoning: Since A(m,4) is on y=4/x, we get 4=4/m, so m=1, that is, the x-coordinate of A is 1. From B(2,n), it can be known that the x-coordinate of B is 2. inequality kx+b-4/x<0 is equivalent to the graph of the linear function being below the graph of the inverse proportional function. According to the image, when 0<x<1, the straight line is below the curve; when 1<x<2, the straight line is above the curve; when x>2, the straight line is again below the curve. At the intersection points, the strict less-than is not satisfied, so the endpoints 1 and 2 are not included.
